headword: {盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}
gloss: the prosperous must decline; all glory is fleeting

definitions.gloss: the prosperous must decline; all glory is fleeting
definitions.explanation: A Buddhist-derived four-character idiom expressing the idea that those who flourish will inevitably fall. One of the most famous phrases from the Tale of the Heike. Composed of 盛者 (the prosperous) + 必衰 (must decline).

examples.japanese: {盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}の{理|ことわり}。
examples.english: The truth that the mighty must fall.

examples.japanese: あの{大企業|だいきぎょう}の{倒産|とうさん}を{見|み}ると、{盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}を{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: Seeing that large company go bankrupt makes you feel that all prosperity must fade.

examples.japanese: {歴史|れきし}を{学|まな}ぶと、{盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}という{言葉|ことば}の{重|おも}みがわかる。
examples.english: When you study history, you understand the weight of the saying 'the prosperous must decline.'

notes:
USAGE:
This is one of the most famous four-character idioms ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) in Japanese. It appears in the opening passage of {平家物語|へいけものがたり} (The Tale of the Heike): 「{祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}の{鐘|かね}の{声|こえ}、{諸行無常|しょぎょうむじょう}の{響|ひび}きあり。{沙羅双樹|さらそうじゅ}の{花|はな}の{色|いろ}、{盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}の{理|ことわり}をあらはす」. Most Japanese people learn this passage in school.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}の{理|ことわり} (the truth that the mighty must fall)
- {盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}を{感|かん}じる (to feel the transience of glory)

RELATED WORDS:
{諸行無常|しょぎょうむじょう} (all things are impermanent) is the companion phrase from the same passage. Together they express the Buddhist view of the impermanence of worldly success.
